parts.title: Part 1 — Introduction and interview
parts.instructions: The examiner will ask general questions about yourself and a few familiar topics. Answer naturally and try to extend each answer with a reason or example. This part lasts 4–5 minutes.

questions.question: Do you work or are you a student?
What do you like most about your job / course?
Let's talk about your hometown. Where is it exactly?
What do you like most about living there?
Has your hometown changed much since you were a child?
Now let's talk about reading. Do you enjoy reading?
What kind of books do you usually read?
Did you read a lot as a child?
Do you prefer reading paper books or e-books? Why?

parts.title: Part 2 — Individual long turn
parts.instructions: You will be given a topic card. You have one minute to prepare and may make notes. Then speak for one to two minutes. Try to keep talking until the examiner stops you.
parts.cue_card_topic: Describe a book you have recently read that you enjoyed.
cue_card_bullets: what kind of book it was
when and where you read it
and explain why you enjoyed it

questions.question: Would you recommend this book to other people? Why or why not?

parts.title: Part 3 — Two-way discussion
parts.instructions: The examiner will ask further questions connected to the Part 2 topic. These are more abstract and require you to explain, compare, and speculate. Try to give extended, well-reasoned answers. This part lasts 4–5 minutes.

questions.question: Do people in your country read as much as they used to?
What kinds of books are most popular with young people today, and why?
Some people say reading fiction is a waste of time compared to reading factual books. What's your opinion?
Do you think digital technology has changed the way people read? In what ways?
How do you think reading habits will change over the next 20 years?
Should governments do more to encourage reading, especially among children?
